issues.legal_issue: A partition of immovable family property is not reopened for the benefit of minor coparceners when the evidence supports a finding that the division was fair and did not harm their interests.
material_facts: The partition of immovable property was made by a separate deed from the partition of movable property.
The lower courts examined the properties allotted to each brother, including their purchase prices and rental or capitalised values, and found the division fair and not detrimental to the minors.
The Supreme Court found no extraordinary or special reason to disturb the lower courts’ concurrent factual findings.
issues.conclusion: The partition of the immovable properties remained binding on the minor plaintiffs, and their challenge to that part of the partition was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: A partition involving minor coparceners binds them when it is made in good faith, fairly, and with their interests taken into account. The Court ordinarily does not disturb concurrent findings of fact absent extraordinary or special reasons.

predicates.partition_challenge_involving_minor_copa: A party challenges a family partition made while minor coparceners were members of the family.
predicates.immovable_property_division_found_fair: The evidence establishes that the division of immovable property was fair and did not harm the minors’ interests.
predicates.no_special_reason_to_disturb_concurrent_: The lower courts made concurrent factual findings and no extraordinary or special reason justifies disturbing them.

issues.definition: When a challenge involving minor coparceners concerns a fair division of immovable property and there is no special reason to disturb concurrent findings, the division remains binding.

issues.legal_issue: A partition of family property that disadvantages minor coparceners may be reopened despite the adults’ consent or the passage of time.
material_facts: The movable-property schedules showed an apparent disparity of about Rs. 10,000 between the brothers’ allotments.
Evidence established that a further Rs. 55,000, intended to be divided between the brothers, had been omitted from the partition deed; the minors’ father did not insist on its division.
The plaintiffs were minor coparceners when the partition occurred, and the omitted and unequal allotments deprived them of part of their shares.
The plaintiffs did not press their allegations of fraud and undue influence before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The movable-property partition was unfair and detrimental to the minors and could be reopened; the Court determined their share and modified the decree to award them Rs. 46,500, with future interest at six per cent per annum until payment.
issues.legal_principle: A consensual partition ordinarily cannot be reopened without proof of fraud, coercion, misrepresentation, or undue influence, for which strict proof is required. But where a partition involving minors is shown to be unjust, unfair, and detrimental to their interests, it may be reopened regardless of the time elapsed; the court must protect the minors, and the party supporting the partition bears the burden of showing it was just and fair. The Court relied on Bishundeo Narain v. Seogeni Rai, Devarajan v. Janaki Ammal, Lal Bahadur Singh v. Sispal Singh, Chanvira 'Pa' v. Da 'Na' 'Va', and Maruti v. Rama.

predicates.partition_challenge_involving_minor_copa: A party challenges a family partition made while minor coparceners were members of the family.
predicates.partition_proved_unjust_or_unfair: The evidence establishes that the partition was unjust or unfair to the minors.
predicates.minors_interests_detrimentally_affected: The partition deprived the minors of property or value to which their interests entitled them.

issues.definition: If a challenged family partition involving minors is proved unjust or unfair and detrimental to their interests, it may be reopened to protect them.

issues.legal_issue: When the movable and immovable property divisions are distinct or separable, a court may preserve the fair division and reopen only the unfair division.
material_facts: The immovable properties were divided under a separate deed from the movable properties, and the movable-property division had occurred at a different time.
The courts found the immovable-property division fair but found an unfair disparity in the movable-property division.
issues.conclusion: The Court left the fair division of immovable properties undisturbed while reopening the unfair division of movable properties.
issues.legal_principle: Where divisions of movable and immovable property are distinct and separable, or occur at different times, a court may maintain the transaction that is fair and reopen only the transaction that is unjust or unfair. The Court applied this proposition alongside the principles governing partitions involving minors, relying on Bishundeo Narain v. Seogeni Rai and the other authorities discussed in its judgment.

rule.if: family_partition_challenge_involving_minors and property_divisions_are_separable and one_division_is_fair and another_division_is_unfair

predicates.family_partition_challenge_involving_min: A party challenges a family partition made while minor coparceners were members of the family.
predicates.property_divisions_are_separable: The divisions of different categories of family property are distinct, separable, or occurred at different times.
predicates.one_division_is_fair: The evidence establishes that one property division was fair.
predicates.another_division_is_unfair: The evidence establishes that a separate property division was unjust or unfair to the minors.

issues.definition: When separable property divisions in a partition involving minors include both a fair division and an unfair one, the fair division is preserved and the unfair division may be reopened.

issues.legal_issue: A minor’s choice of property in a partition does not by itself justify reopening the partition when the choice was reasonably made on the information available at the time.
material_facts: The minors’ father selected shares in one company rather than shares in another company after receiving information that the latter shares were trading below their paid-up value and paying a small dividend.
The shares he did not select rose substantially years later because of circumstances he could not have foreseen.
The evidence did not establish that the allocation of the shares was unjust or unequal when made.
issues.conclusion: The allocation of the company shares was not unfair or unequal and did not justify reopening that part of the movable-property division.
issues.legal_principle: A choice made in good faith on the information reasonably available at the time is not enough to reopen a partition merely because it later proves mistaken or less advantageous. The Court applied the principles for assessing whether a partition was fair to minors, including the distinction between an unfair division and an error of judgment.

predicates.partition_challenge_involving_minor_copa: A party challenges a family partition made while minor coparceners were members of the family.
predicates.guardian_selected_property_on_informatio: The minors’ guardian selected an item of property using the information available when the partition was made.
predicates.later_disadvantage_was_unforeseeable: The property later became less advantageous because of circumstances that could not reasonably have been foreseen at the time.
predicates.allocation_was_not_unfair_when_made: The evidence does not establish that the allocation was unfair or unequal when it was made.

issues.definition: A later unforeseen disadvantage does not justify reopening a partition when a guardian made a reasonable property selection on the information then available and the allocation was not unfair when made.

issues.legal_issue: A court may award a quantified monetary share instead of ordering a full repartition and appointing a commissioner when the minors’ shares can be determined in money and a full inquiry would prolong litigation.
material_facts: The partition had taken place many years before the suit, and reconstructing the assets and their values at that time would be difficult.
The minors’ shares in the movable-property disparity could be calculated in money from the evidence.

The High Court quantified the disparity but the Supreme Court found its calculation insufficient and determined a higher amount, adding interest for the period of deprivation and providing for future interest.
The Court considered that appointing a commissioner to reopen the entire partition would not serve the minors’ interests or the interests of justice.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to order appointment of a commissioner or full repartition and instead awarded the plaintiffs Rs. 46,500, with future interest at six per cent per annum until payment.
issues.legal_principle: A court may use a quantified monetary award rather than reopen an entire partition when the minors’ shares are readily ascertainable in money, particularly where a full inquiry into a long-past division would be impracticable or cause protracted litigation. The remedy should protect the minors’ interests and secure their just share.

predicates.partition_challenge_involving_minors: A party challenges a family partition made while minor coparceners were members of the family.
predicates.minors_share_readily_quantifiable_in_mon: The evidence permits the minors’ share to be determined in monetary terms without a full repartition.
predicates.full_repartition_would_be_impracticable_: Reconstructing and dividing the property would be impracticable or would prolong litigation.

issues.definition: When minors’ shares can be determined in money and a full repartition would be impracticable or prolong litigation, the court may award a quantified monetary amount instead.
